RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: a slave asks for his freedom
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A slave of the colony stands before the lord and asks to be made free.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} was not called. {PETITIONER_pronoun} came anyway, and stood where the free people stand, and asked for the one thing a slave is not supposed to ask for.

Nobody in the hall is speaking for {PETITIONER_objective}. Nobody has to. The question is on the floor, in front of everyone, and it will be answered one way or the other.

How does the lord rule?

li.label: Rule that a slave is a slave, and send {PETITIONER_objective} back to work
Move on to the next case

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: what he left on the field
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist maimed fighting for the colony asks the lord what it was worth.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} has killed {KILLS} people for this colony and carries the proof: something did not grow back. {PETITIONER_pronoun} is not asking for pity. {PETITIONER_pronoun} is asking what the lord thinks it was worth, and has come with three answers the lord could give.

Take {WORK} off {PETITIONER_objective}, which {PETITIONER_pronoun} was never good at and now hates. Or {SILVER} silver, which says it plainly. Or a word before the court, which costs nothing and {PETITIONER_pronoun} will notice that it cost nothing.

How does the lord rule?

li.label: Honour {PETITIONER_labelShort} before the court, and nothing more
li.pastLabel: honoured for the wound, and nothing more
